subject: TrustBound connectivity — IP ownership, firewall guardrails, and outbound controls
messages:
From: Alan Wu <alan.wu@medicorp.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: TrustBound connectivity — requirements and questions

Laura / team,

Thanks for taking this through the NetworkSec review. We are preparing our private deployment checklist for the Redwood runtime and need concrete answers on IP ownership, firewall rules, and outbound/egress controls so we can complete our internal SOC checklist. High level asks: 

- Can you confirm whether Redwood provides a set of static egress IPs we can allowlist, or do you require customer-managed NAT (customer-owned egress IPs)?
- If Redwood provides IPs, what is the stabilization/rotation cadence and are there per-region pools?
- Which outbound ports and protocols must be permitted from our private runtime to Redwood control/telemetry endpoints?
- Is SNI-based FQDN allowlisting supported if we cannot permit raw IP ranges?
- Do you support mutual TLS for control-plane connections, and can you provide certificate pins or fingerprints for verification?
- What telemetry/audit evidence (connection logs, cert chain) can Redwood provide during onboarding and for periodic audits?

We attached our current network diagram and questionnaire to this message. We're aiming to lock the network policy by EOW so we can schedule a connectivity test next week.

Attachments: MedCorp_Network_Diagram.pdf (diagram stub), MedCorp_Questionnaire.xlsx (network questionnaire stub)

Thanks,
Alan Wu
Network Security — MediCorp
alan.wu@medicorp.com

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TrustBound connectivity — requirements and questions

Alan — thanks for the clear list and the attachments. Sharing a proposed approach and next steps below so we can converge quickly.

Summary of our deployment options (what we typically offer for private endpoints):

1) Customer-managed egress (recommended for regulated environments)
   - Customer keeps control of outbound NAT (single or per-region SNAT) and allowlists Redwood inbound addresses for control-plane connections.
   - Benefit: you retain ownership of egress IPs and control rotation cadence. Redwood provides hostnames and short-lived cert-based auth for the control plane.

2) Redwood-managed egress (reserved, static pool)
   - For customers who cannot run a NAT, Redwood can assign a reserved egress pool for your deployment. We provide a published list of IPs to add to your firewall.
   - Note: we operate a rotation process for ephemeral sub-pools; however reserved pools for private deployments are treated as stable for the term of the contract unless emergency rotation is required.

Technical answers to your specific questions:
- Static egress IPs: yes — available via Redwood-managed reserved pools for private deployments. If you prefer crisp ownership, choose customer-managed egress so MediCorp owns the SNAT IPs.
- Rotation cadence: Redwood-managed reserved pools are rotated only in exceptional circumstances; normal rotation cadence applies to shared ephemeral pools (weekly rolling updates). We'll provide advance notice and an IP escrow process for reserved pools.
- Ports/protocols: allow outbound TCP 443 (HTTPS) to the control-plane FQDNs. Additionally, allow outbound TCP 443 to telemetry endpoints. We do not require other ports for control/management traffic.
- SNI allowlisting: supported. If your firewall supports SNI inspection, you can allow FQDNs instead of IP ranges.
- mTLS: supported for control-plane connections. We can provide certificate fingerprints and a short-lived client cert exchange for initial bootstrap.
- Audit/telemetry: we can provide connection logs (timestamps, source IP, destination FQDN, TLS fingerprint) for onboarding evidence and a periodic export for audits.

Proposed next steps and timeline:
- 1) David to produce a candidate IP list (Redwood-managed) + rotation SOP by EOD (we'll create INF-9423).
- 2) MediCorp to confirm preference (customer-owned SNAT vs Redwood-managed reserved pool) by Wed 8/31 EOD.
- 3) Schedule a 30-min connectivity canary on Thur 9/2 (we will coordinate with your ops window).
- 4) Exchange mTLS cert fingerprints and finalize firewall rules; Redwood will provide an evidence bundle post-canary.

Looping in David (networking) and Marissa (CS/ops) to coordinate technical details and the runbook.

— Laura Bennett
Manager, Partner Engineering — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Alan — quick technical follow-up with concrete artifacts attached.

Concrete items: 
- Recommended firewall allowlist (minimum): outbound TCP 443 to the following FQDN patterns: api.redwood-inference.internal, telemetry.redwood-inference.internal, auth.redwood-inference.internal. If SNI-only inspection is in use, permit the matching SANs for those hostnames.
- Candidate Redwood-managed reserved egress ranges (subject to contract & region): 54.210.23.0/24, 54.210.24.0/25. These ranges are provisioned as your private deployment's dedicated egress pool and will be delivered to you as a signed manifest.
- Ephemeral pool behavior: shared ephemeral pool IPs rotate on a weekly rolling cadence; reserved pools for private deployments are marked "stable" in the manifest and rotation only occurs for security incidents or coordinated maintenance (we will provide 7-day notice for planned changes).
- mTLS/fingerprint exchange: we will provision a short-lived client cert for your runtime to present to the control plane during the initial bootstrap. Fingerprints and cert metadata will be included in the onboarding bundle.
- Audit exports: we can push connection logs to an S3-compatible endpoint you provide or share a signed CSV bundle after the canary.

Operational asks for MediCorp before the canary:
1) Confirm whether you want Redwood-managed reserved pool or to preserve your own SNAT IPs.
2) If you choose customer SNAT, provide the post-NAT egress IPs and a point-of-contact for rotation windows.
3) Confirm a maintenance window for Thurs 9/2 02:00–04:00 UTC for our canary.

Attachment: egress-ip-range.csv (stub) — contains candidate CIDRs and notes.

—David Kim
